speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent; could you please tell me when your gait and limb coordination issues first started, and if they have been getting worse over time?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any other symptoms like dizziness, slurred speech, or vision changes alongside this clumsiness? Also, do you have a history of alcohol use or any recent head injuries?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and recent initiation of natalizumab, have you experienced any new headaches, confusion, or focal neurological symptoms like weakness? I need to rule out complications from your medication, so I will REQUEST TEST: Brain_MRI_with_contrast.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature Normothermic, Blood Pressure Within normal range, Heart Rate Within normal range, Respiratory Rate Within normal range. Neurological Examination: Ataxic gait noted; Right Upper Limb Strength 4/5; Evidence of ataxia on coordination tests. MRI Brain Findings: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). Comments: T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI findings of multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement are highly indicative of Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML) associated with your natalizumab treatment. Given your significant Crohn's history and the severity of these findings, I need to confirm your current immune status. Do you know your current CD4 count or have you had any recent viral infections?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you haven't had a fever, but your MRI confirms Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy, a serious infection of the brain linked to your natalizumab treatment. Since this condition is diagnosed based on the characteristic MRI findings and your clinical presentation, no further questions are needed to confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML)
